preamble: Loss of the voiced palatal affricate [dʒ] between vowels was part of the general weakening of single intervocalic stops in Middle Indo-Aryan. In Maharashtri and the Jain Prakrits, intervocalic k, g, c, j, t and d were usually elided, leaving the surrounding vowels in hiatus (sometimes bridged by a light glide, the ya-śruti, in Jain spelling). Hemacandra's grammar (1.177) states the rule but marks it as usual rather than exceptionless, and Sauraseni kept intervocalic -d- where Maharashtri dropped it. The Old Indo-Aryan sound is written j and is transcribed [dʒ] here, following the atlas's existing Indo-Aryan entries; Wiktionary transcribes it as [dʑ].

examples.note: The intervocalic affricate is lost and the two vowels stand in hiatus.

examples.to: Ardhamagadhi and Jain Maharashtri 𑀭𑀸𑀅 rāa (also spelled 𑀭𑀸𑀬 rāya)
examples.note: The spelling with y is the ya-śruti hiatus glide of Jain manuscripts, not a continuation of the affricate.
The Prakrit form was borrowed into Dravidian as Kannada and Tulu bōna and Telugu bōnamu.
